subject: Future Tech
title: Landing on Mars
description: A quick win: understand Landing on Mars.

hook.text: Mars has just enough atmosphere to cause problems but not enough to slow a heavy spacecraft. Landing is a nightmare.

buildup.text: Parachutes work on Mars, but only for small payloads. The thin air can't slow anything heavier than a rover.

discovery.text: NASA's sky crane lowered Curiosity and Perseverance on cables from a hovering platform. It worked but can't scale.

twist.text: Human landers weigh 20+ tons. No existing Mars landing system handles that mass. New retro-propulsion tech is needed.

climax.text: SpaceX plans to land Starship on Mars using its engines alone, belly-flopping through the thin atmosphere first.

punchline.text: Getting to Mars is easy. Stopping is the hard part.

quiz.question: Why can't parachutes alone land heavy spacecraft on Mars?
options: The atmosphere is too thin for heavy loads
